question: In a certain code language, 'COFFEE' is coded as '40', 'LEMON' is coded as '59', and 'GINGER' is coded as '60'. How will 'TEA' be coded in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8564f6202cca34055eb3fbabcf7d02094467c98de952b91901a5c06d2aaa5af6.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: Sum of the place value = Number.

Here,

'COFFEE' is coded as '40'.

⇒ C(3) + O(15) + F(6) + F(6) + E(5) + E(5)

⇒ 3 + 15 + 6 + 6 + 5 + 5 = 40.

And, 'LEMON' is coded as '59'.

⇒ L(12) + E(5) + M(13) + O(15) + N(14)

⇒ 12 + 5 + 13 + 15 + 14 = 59.

'GINGER' is coded as '60'

⇒ G(7) + I(9) + N(14) + G(7) + E(5) + R(18)

⇒ 7 + 9 + 14 + 7 + 5 + 18 = 60.

Similarly, for **'TEA'**

**⇒ T(20) + E(5) + A(1)**

**⇒ 20 + 5 + 1 = 26.**

So, 'TEA' will be coded as '26'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
